_readme: URL -> { date, title, filePath } recorded the first time that URL was ever emitted into a WXR file. WordPress recognizes an already-imported page by matching its TITLE AND its DATE together (see "How WordPress decides..." in tools/wxr/README.md). "date" holds ONE OF TWO shapes, and the shape itself is the signal for which one you have: (1) a bare calendar date, "YYYY-MM-DD" — a RESERVATION, not a record. This URL has never been confirmed against a live WordPress post; generate.js will emit it at midnight UTC, which is fine because nobody has published this page yet, so no live timestamp exists yet to disagree with it. (2) a full ISO-8601 datetime with a UTC offset, e.g. "2026-09-10T20:03:42+00:00" — a HARVESTED value, copied verbatim (including the offset) from that exact page's live RankMath JSON-LD "datePublished" field. Every wave-1 URL (see tools/wxr/waves.json wave "1") was corrected to this shape on 2026-09-14 after the bare-midnight dates were found to have drifted from what WordPress actually put on the live pages once they were published — the fix that shape (2) exists to make permanent. generate.js reads either shape the same way: a bare date gets "T00:00:00Z" appended, a full ISO string is parsed as-is (see parseRegistryDateString). IMPORTANT — why bare dates drift and full ones don't: this tool always imports pages as `<wp:status>draft</wp:status>` (see tools/wxr/lib/wxr-xml.js and the README's "What it does"). A WordPress draft does not keep the wp:post_date this tool wrote as its real "this is when it went live" date — internally a draft's post_date is treated as unset, and the moment a human clicks Publish on it, WordPress stamps that literal moment as the post's real post_date/ post_date_gmt, overwriting whatever this tool imported it with. So a date recorded here is only ever guaranteed to still be accurate for a URL that has NEVER been published in WordPress yet (shape 1, correctly). The instant a human publishes it, this tool's stamped date silently goes stale — it is still remembered here, but it no longer matches the live page, exactly the drift that hit all 17 wave-1 URLs (16 of them share 2026-09-10T20:03:42+00:00; one, /pet-guides/pet-travel/, was republished separately at 2026-09-10T20:20:17+00:00 — always harvest per-URL, never assume one page's value for another). If this happens again for a URL already in this file: open the live page, read `datePublished` out of its RankMath JSON-LD (view source or a console `document.querySelectorAll('script[type="application/ld+json"]')` search — the same way the 2026-09-14 correction was harvested), and hand-edit just that entry's "date" to the exact live string, offset included; generate.js also now warns automatically the moment a run re-emits a URL whose registry date is still bare (see warnAboutUnharvestedDates in generate.js and "Re-harvesting a drifted date" in tools/wxr/README.md) so this cannot rot silently again. generate.js appends one new bare-date entry automatically (via --date) the first time a URL needs one; it never rewrites an entry that already exists on its own — if the current H1 for a URL no longer matches the recorded title, generate.js stops with an error instead of guessing which one is right (silently picking either one reopens the exact duplicate-page bug this file exists to prevent). "filePath" is only used to notice when a URL itself has been renamed in content/ (the same file now defines a different URL) — see "A page's URL changing" in tools/wxr/README.md. Commit this file whenever generate.js reports it added new entries, or whenever you hand-correct a drifted date. To correct a mistake before anything has actually been imported into WordPress, it is safe to hand-edit an entry directly — it is plain JSON; correcting a drifted live date is exactly as safe, since this file is a record of fact for WordPress's benefit, not an input WordPress reads live.
